shipped_rows.title_o: Fast But Fleeting: Adaptive Motor Learning Processes Associated with Aging and Cognitive Decline

blind_target.authors: Vandevoorde K, Orban de Xivry JJ.
blind_target.title: Internal model recalibration does not deteriorate with age while motor adaptation does.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Therefore, we set out to measure both implicit adaptation and its retention via spontaneous recovery in a single force-ﬁeld paradigm in both healthy young and older adults to test four different hypotheses, reﬂecting previous research: 1) implicit adaptation levels at the end of the adaptation period are similar across age groups (27), 2) spontaneous recovery is larger in young than in older participants (37), 3) implicit adaptation at the end of the adaptation period is correlated with the amount of spontaneous recovery (45), and 4) as suggested by Trewartha and colleagues, spontaneous recovery is related to explicit memory processes such as working memory capacity.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Across age groups, we observed little difference in performance in this task. Both total adaptation and implicit adaptation were not impaired in older adults compared with their younger controls.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Hypothesis 1 explicitly re-tests reference 27: preserved implicit adaptation with age. New sample shows the same finding.

blind_target.authors: McDougle SD, Bond KM, Taylor JA.
blind_target.title: Explicit and implicit processes constitute the fast and slow processes of sensorimotor learning.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Therefore, we set out to measure both implicit adaptation and its retention via spontaneous recovery in a single force-ﬁeld paradigm in both healthy young and older adults to test four different hypotheses, reﬂecting previous research: 1) implicit adaptation levels at the end of the adaptation period are similar across age groups (27), 2) spontaneous recovery is larger in young than in older participants (37), 3) implicit adaptation at the end of the adaptation period is correlated with the amount of spontaneous recovery (45), and 4) as suggested by Trewartha and colleagues, spontaneous recovery is related to explicit memory processes such as working memory capacity.
blind_target.outcome_quote: This is consistent with the correlation between the amount of implicit adaptation during learning and the amount of spontaneous recovery (Fig. 6). This is also consistent with the ﬁndings of McDougle et al. (45).
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Hypothesis 3 explicitly re-tests reference 45 linking implicit adaptation to spontaneous recovery; discussion explicitly agrees.

luna_triage.reason: The source specifies and tests hypothesis 1, that implicit adaptation is similar across age groups, explicitly grounding it in Vandevoorde et al. (27). The Discussion reports no impairment of implicit adaptation in older adults. The only shipped original is Trewartha et al. (2014), row 2324, which is a different work and does not represent Vandevoorde et al. (2019).
